question: A patient arrives at the emergency unit with a deep dog bite on the forearm. Which assessment finding requires the most urgent escalation to a physician?

options.A: Moderate localized redness spanning two centimeters around the edges
options.B: Mild oozing of serosanguineous fluid from the puncture site
options.C: Inability to move the fingers and absent distal pulse
options.D: Patient reporting mild anxiety and emotional distress about the event

explanation: Loss of movement and absent pulses indicate acute neurovascular or tendon compromise, which is a surgical emergency. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T11#GNS221_U3_T11_h3)

question: What is a major environmental drawback of operating a poorly maintained low-temperature incinerator?

options.A: It turns all hazardous waste into harmless drinking water
options.B: It completely freezes the surrounding soil layers
options.C: It emits toxic pollutants like dioxins and furans into the air
options.D: It increases the local municipal electricity supply voltage

explanation: Incomplete combustion at low temperatures releases hazardous airborne chemical pollutants that harm public health. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h7)

question: Which class of medication is commonly prescribed as a first-line treatment for chronic neuropathic pain?

options.A: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
options.B: Loop diuretics and potassium supplements
options.C: Inhaled short-acting bronchodilators
options.D: Gabapentinoids and tricyclic antidepressants

explanation: Neuropathic pain is driven by abnormal neuronal firing, making medications like gabapentin and amitriptyline much more effective than standard analgesics. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of the FAST exam in trauma and critical care?

options.A: Measuring exact intracardiac pressures
options.B: Screening for intracranial hemorrhage
options.C: Calculating precise cardiac output rates
options.D: Detecting free fluid in body cavities

explanation: The FAST scan is a rapid bedside ultrasound tool designed to identify intraperitoneal, pericardial, or pleural hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which laboratory test is specifically used to monitor therapeutic heparin therapy?

options.A: Partial Thromboplastin Time (PTT)
options.B: Prothrombin Time (PT)
options.C: International Normalized Ratio (INR)
options.D: Mean Corpuscular Volume (MCV)

explanation: PTT evaluates the intrinsic coagulation pathway and is the standard test utilized to monitor unfractionated heparin infusions. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T7#GNS123_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is the minimum amount of time a diaphragm must remain in the vagina after intercourse?

options.A: Twenty-four hours
options.B: Six hours
options.C: One hour
options.D: Twelve hours

explanation: Leaving the diaphragm in place for at least six hours post-coitus gives the spermicide adequate time to destroy all viable sperm. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h6)

question: Why is a patient asked to empty her bladder immediately before undergoing an MVA?

options.A: To displace the uterus forward and reduce discomfort
options.B: To prevent urinary tract infections during surgery
options.C: To speed up the absorption of oral antibiotic prophylaxis
options.D: To collect a routine midstream urine sample

explanation: An empty bladder moves out of the surgical path, tilts the uterus into a more favorable position, and lowers procedural pain. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h4)

question: Which component of semen is eliminated immediately following a vasectomy?

options.A: Spermatozoa
options.B: Prostatic fluid
options.C: Mucus secretions
options.D: Seminal vesicle fluid

explanation: The mechanical block prevents sperm from entering the ejaculate, while all glandular fluids that make up semen remain present. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T020#GNS226_U6_T020_h3)

question: What hormonal shift immediately triggers the onset of copious milk production following delivery of the placenta?

options.A: A sharp surge in maternal serum progesterone levels
options.B: A massive spike in anterior pituitary luteinizing hormone
options.C: A sudden drop in circulating placental estrogen and progesterone
options.D: A complete cessation of maternal prolactin secretion

explanation: High placental hormone levels block milk synthesis during pregnancy; their expulsion at birth removes this block, enabling prolactin action. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h6)

question: Which medical specialist leads the multidisciplinary rehabilitation team?

options.A: General practitioner
options.B: Physiatrist
options.C: Neurologist
options.D: Orthopedic surgeon

explanation: A physiatrist is a physician who specializes specifically in physical medicine and rehabilitation to direct comprehensive recovery plans. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T5#GNS123_U6_T5_h2)

question: How does effective leadership by nursing personnel directly impact institutional waste management compliance?

options.A: By manufacturing color-coded bin liners locally
options.B: By drafting national environmental health legislation
options.C: By personally operating the central hospital incinerator daily
options.D: By ensuring consistent bedside sorting and proper maintenance of ward supplies

explanation: Nurses drive daily compliance and maintain adequate supply levels of bins and safety boxes at the point of care. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h7)
